source.author: Al Brooks
source.chapter_title: Bar Counting: High and Low 1, 2, 3, and 4 Patterns and ABC Corrections

conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode; sides field states mirrored/same

candidates.name: HighLowBarCounter
candidates.quote: the first bar whose high is above the high of the prior bar is a high 1, and this ends the first leg of the sideways or down move ... label the next occurrence of a bar with a high above the high of the prior bar as a high 2, ending the second leg.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a persistent counter (highCount) of completed pullback legs since the trend last made a fresh N-bar high. Each bar whose high exceeds the immediately preceding bar's high ('count-worthy') advances the count by one -- but only once the pullback has made a new low since the previous count-worthy bar (otherwise it is a retest of the same leg, not a new one). The count resets to 0 the instant price closes at a fresh N-bar high (the pullback is over, the trend resumed). This sharpens trends/00_front_matter.json's PullbackLegCounter (T00-19, graded research there) into a concrete, swing-pivot-free rule.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (state primitive underlying every high/low N setup below)

complexity.reason: a cross-bar persistent counter plus a remembered signal-bar low and a rolling N-bar-highest reset test -- no swing-pivot or trend-line detection required

notes: resetLookback stands in for 'the trend's prior extreme'; Brooks fixes no window for this, so 20 is reused from chapter 13's unrelated EMA-gap setup purely for a consistent default, not because the book ties the two together.
Downgrades T00-19's 'research' grade to 'moderate' by replacing its vague reset condition with a concrete N-bar-high test; the dedup pass should reconcile the two definitions.

ABC correction terminology maps directly onto this counter: leg A = the run down to the count-1 (high 1 / B point) bar, leg B = the failed bounce, leg C = the run down to the count-2 (high 2) bar, whose breakout is the ABC entry -- ABC is not a separate mechanism, just chapter 17's name for a high 2 / low 2.

candidates.name: TrendLineBreakConfirmsCount
candidates.quote: There needs to be at least a tiny trend line break between the high 1 and the high 2 to indicate that the trend traders are still active. Without this, do not yet look to buy
candidates.description: Require at least a minor trend-line break between successive counted bars before trusting the next count number as tradable; without one, treat the sequence as a single complex leg (a channel) rather than an advancing count.
candidates.pseudocode: microTrendLineBroken(sinceLastSignal) -> countIsTradable = true; else countIsTradable = false

complexity.reason: needs micro trend-line projection from pivots between two counted bars

candidates.name: HighOneEntry
candidates.quote: A high 1 long trade after the initial spike up in a new bull trend has a high probability of being at least a successful swing trade.
candidates.description: Buy one tick above the high of the signal bar that just advanced HighLowBarCounter to 1.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the high 1 signal bar

complexity.reason: trivial once the counter's per-bar transition is known, but that transition itself is moderate (R17-01)

notes: Reliable mainly in the spike phase of a strong trend and after the initial spike of a brand-new trend; see R17-07/R17-08 for the required filters.
Mirrors to Low 1 in a bear trend.

candidates.name: HighTwoEntry
candidates.quote: The bulls will see the setup as two attempts to drive the market down where both failed, so they will buy the high 2 long.
candidates.description: Buy one tick above the high of the signal bar that just advanced HighLowBarCounter to 2.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the high 2 signal bar

complexity.reason: trivial once the counter's per-bar transition is known, but that transition itself is moderate (R17-01)

notes: One of the most reliable with-trend setups per the book, especially in a bull trend rather than a trading range (see R17-11 for the trading-range fade variant). Mirrors to Low 2 in a bear trend, and is the entry the book calls an ABC correction.

candidates.name: HighThreeWedgeEntry
candidates.quote: High 3 and low 3 patterns should be traded like wedges (or a traditional triangle, if the pattern is mostly horizontal) because functionally they are the same.
candidates.description: Buy one tick above the high of the signal bar that just advanced HighLowBarCounter to 3; functionally a wedge/triangle bull-flag entry (three pushes down).
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the high 3 signal bar

complexity.reason: trivial once the counter's per-bar transition is known; the book's wedge-shape refinement is not separately encoded here

notes: Preferred over waiting for a high 4 when the breakout below the failed high 2 was not strong (see R17-08's momentum read); risky when that breakout was a strong bear spike, in which case wait for high 4 (R17-06).

candidates.name: HighFourEntry
candidates.quote: Whenever there is a strong breakout below a high 2 or wedge (high 3) buy signal bar, the market usually will have at least two more pushes down ... a high 4 pullback.
candidates.description: Buy one tick above the high of the signal bar that just advanced HighLowBarCounter to 4.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the high 4 signal bar

complexity.reason: trivial once the counter's per-bar transition is known

notes: If the high 4 fails (price falls below its signal-bar low after triggering), the book says the market is more likely no longer a bull pullback but a bear swing (see R17-13's reversal-on-opposing-trigger candidate).

candidates.name: ClimaxFilterBlocksCountEntry
candidates.quote: The final component is a filter -- do not take a high 1 following a significant buy climax, and don't take a low 1 short after a significant sell climax.
candidates.description: Never take a High 1 buy after a significant recent buy climax, nor a Low 1 short after a significant sell climax -- a climax exhausts the very trend the count is supposed to continue.

complexity.reason: 'climax' needs a design decision (large-range/exhaustion-bar detection); already defined as a primitive in the Trends volume, not redefined here

notes: Climax primitive is defined in trends chapter 2 (trend bars, doji bars, and climaxes).

candidates.name: SpikeAndTrendRequiredForCount
candidates.quote: For traders to buy a high 1, they need a strong bull spike and a bull trend, not simply a spike up within a trading range.
candidates.description: Require both a strong recent spike (several consecutive trend bars with small overlap) and an established trend (not merely a trading-range spike) before trusting a High 1/2 or Low 1/2 entry.

complexity.reason: compound spike detection plus a trend-strength read from the AlwaysInDirection family

notes: Same spike concept as R05-07/R05-10 (ranges chapter 5); dedup pass should compare parameters.

candidates.name: TrendDirectionGateForCounts
candidates.quote: If the market is in a clear bull trend, do not look for low 1 or low 2 shorts, because those are setups only in bear trends and trading ranges. If the market is in a clear bear trend, do not look for high 1 or high 2 buys
candidates.description: Block High 1/2 buy setups while in a clear bear trend, and Low 1/2 short setups while in a clear bull trend; both remain valid inside a trading range.
candidates.pseudocode: !clearBearTrend() -> allow R17-03/R17-04 (mirrored: !clearBullTrend() -> allow the low-side entries)

complexity.reason: depends on the AlwaysInDirection trend-classification primitive, itself a design decision

candidates.name: FadeCountBreakoutWithStrongTrend
candidates.quote: if the market is in a bear trend, you can often look to short above the high of the prior bar because buying a high 1 in a bear trend is a low-probability trade ... you can look to sell above the high of any bar in a strong bear trend or in a bear channel
candidates.description: In a strong, established trend, fade every opposite-direction count-worthy bar directly instead of waiting for a labeled Low N/High N: short at (or a few ticks above) the high of any bar in a strong bear trend or bear channel; mirrored, buy at (or a few ticks below) the low of any bar in a strong bull trend or bull channel.
candidates.pseudocode: strongBearTrendOrChannel() && high[0] > high[1] -> sell limit at high[1] + fadeOffsetTicks * tickSize, expecting the break to fail
candidates.book_order_type: sell limit at/above the prior bar's high (a deliberate fade of the High 1 buy setup)

complexity.reason: depends on the AlwaysInLong/AlwaysInShort family to classify 'strong trend or channel'

notes: This is the same high[0] > high[1] trigger as R17-01, traded in the opposite direction because the trend context reverses which side is favored.

candidates.name: TradingRangeBoundaryCountFade
candidates.quote: when you are buying a high 2 in a trading range, you are usually looking to buy a reversal where the setup is below the moving average and near the bottom of the range ... it is risky to buy a high 2 above the moving average and near the high of the trading range ... you should instead consider shorting using a limit order at or above the high of the high 2 signal bar.
candidates.description: In a trading-range context, a High 2 setup that forms above the EMA and near the top of the range is more likely to fail; fade it instead with a limit short at/above the signal bar's high (mirrored: a Low 2 near the bottom of the range in a trading range is a buy fade).
candidates.pseudocode: isTradingRange() && R17-04[0] && close[0] > ema(emaLength) && close[0] >= (rangeHigh - nearTopFraction * (rangeHigh - rangeLow)) -> sell limit at signal bar high instead of buying it
candidates.book_order_type: sell limit at/above the high 2 signal bar's high

complexity.reason: 'trading range' has no agreed mechanical definition; the EMA-side and near-boundary tests are otherwise concrete

candidates.name: FailedCountSetupEarlyExit
candidates.quote: Once a high 2 long triggers in a bull trend or in a trading range, if the market then reverses and trades below the low of the pattern before reaching at least a scalper's profit, the high 2 buy has failed.
candidates.description: Exit a High N long (or Low N short) if price trades back below (above) the signal bar's low (high) before the position has reached at least a minimal scalper's profit.
candidates.pseudocode: low[0] < R17-01.signalLow && ctx.OpenPositionProfit() < scalpProfitTicks * tickSize * bigPointValue -> exit
candidates.book_order_type: protective stop below the signal bar's low

complexity.reason: needs the remembered signal-bar extreme from R17-01 plus an open-profit read

notes: A failed count usually evolves into the next count number (a failed high 2 leads to a high 3 or high 4 attempt), which is simply R17-01 continuing to advance -- no separate candidate needed for that.

candidates.name: ReverseOnOpposingCountTrigger
candidates.quote: if you ever buy early, always get out and even reverse if the market triggers a low 2 or 3 short, especially if there is a strong bear signal bar ... if you short a strong bull trend, always get out if a high 2 or 3 triggers
candidates.description: While long against a developing opposite trend, exit (and optionally reverse) the moment an opposing Low 2/Low 3 short setup itself triggers; mirrored for a short caught by a High 2/High 3 trigger.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && (LowTwoEntryTriggered[0] || LowThreeEntryTriggered[0]) -> exit long (optionally reverse to short)
candidates.book_order_type: market/stop exit (and reversal) on the opposing signal's trigger

complexity.reason: position-state read combined with the mirrored counter's own trigger, both already defined elsewhere

notes: Kindred to R05-06's reversal permission, but gated on an opposing bar-count trigger instead of a reversal-bar pattern.

candidates.name: SmallSignalBarWiderProtectiveStop
candidates.quote: If the signal bar is particularly small, especially if it is a doji, sometimes the entry bar will quickly reverse into an outside bar, running the protective stops ... it is often best to place your protective stop at more than one tick beyond the signal bar (maybe three ticks, but no more than a total of eight ticks from your entry
candidates.description: When the High N/Low N signal bar is small (near-doji), widen the protective stop to a few ticks beyond the signal bar's extreme instead of exactly one tick, capped at a maximum total distance from the entry price.
candidates.pseudocode: signalBarRange = high[1] - low[1]; stopOffsetTicks = (signalBarRange <= smallBarMaxTicks * tickSize) ? widerStopTicks : 1; stopPrice = max(R17-01.signalLow - stopOffsetTicks * tickSize, ctx.EntryPrice() - maxStopTicks * tickSize)
candidates.book_order_type: protective stop a few ticks beyond a small/doji signal bar, capped in total distance from entry

complexity.reason: needs the signal bar's own range plus the entry price to apply the cap

notes: The book's 8-tick cap is calibrated to the 5 minute Emini's roughly 10-point average range; treated here as a plain parameter.

candidates.name: CorrectionAdequacyBeforeReCounting
candidates.quote: in general the correction should have two clear legs and have at least about half as many bars as the wedge
candidates.description: After a climax or wedge extreme, require the corrective move to run at least half as many bars as the pattern it is correcting, and to show two clear legs, before treating a subsequent count as tradable.
candidates.pseudocode: correctionBars >= minCorrectionFraction * patternBars && R17-01.highCount >= 2 -> allow re-counting

complexity.reason: needs the bar-span of the pattern being corrected, which requires pivot/wedge detection

notes: Same guideline as chapter 16's R16-02, restated here specifically for a wedge/climax low.

candidates.name: CountertrendMicroSignalMustFailFirst
candidates.quote: High 1 and low 1 patterns are with-trend setups, so if one occurs within a pullback in a trend but in the direction of the pullback and not the trend, do not take the trade. Instead, wait for it to fail and then enter with the trend on the breakout pullback.
candidates.description: If a High 1/Low 1-shaped bar forms in the direction of a pullback (against the larger trend) rather than with the trend, do not trade it directly; require it to fail first, then take the resulting with-trend breakout-pullback entry instead.
candidates.pseudocode: counterTrendCountBar(R17-01) -> do not enter directly; wait for FailedBreakoutReversalEntry-style continuation with the trend
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (redirects the trade to the with-trend breakout-pullback entry)

complexity.reason: requires knowing the larger trend direction plus the breakout-pullback primitives from chapter 5

candidates.name: MeasuredMoveFromFailedCountBreakout
candidates.quote: If instead there is a large bear breakout bar or two, this increases the odds that there will be at least two more legs down, and traders should wait for the high 4 before looking to buy. In this case, the breakout bar is likely to become a measuring gap and lead to a measured move down.
candidates.description: When a failed High 2 breaks down with a strong (measuring-gap) bar, project a measured-move target using the height of the failed pattern.
candidates.book_order_type: profit-taking limit at the measured-move target

complexity.reason: needs the failed pattern's height plus measuring-gap-bar classification, both requiring pivot bookkeeping

notes: Overlaps chapter 16's R16-03 and chapter 8's measured-move candidates; dedup pass should compare.

rejected.quote: It is not worth looking at the higher time frame charts since the trades are evident on the 5 minute chart and you risk distracting yourself looking for rare signals and missing too many 5 minute signals.
rejected.reason: meta-commentary against consulting a higher timeframe chart at all; not itself a bar-level condition, and would require a second bar series if it were

rejected.quote: it is helpful to study the chart from different perspectives, like using a bar chart or an inverse chart.
rejected.reason: requires a second synthetic representation (an inverse ETF/chart) not part of the engine's single OHLCV bar series

rejected.quote: Look at the inset of the 1 minute chart. The 5 minute signal bar was made up of the five 1 minute bars between the dashed lines
rejected.reason: requires a second, faster-timeframe bar series (1 minute) alongside the strategy's own bars

chapter_summary: The trilogy's most mechanizable chapter: formalizes the High 1/2/3/4 and Low 1/2/3/4 bar-counting setups (with ABC corrections as just the book's name for a high 2/low 2) as a single persistent leg counter. R17-01 gives a concrete, swing-pivot-free definition -- advance the count on each higher-high bar that follows a new low since the last counted bar, reset on a fresh N-bar high -- which sharpens the existing PullbackLegCounter/LegDefinition primitives (graded research elsewhere) down to moderate. From it follow four graduated entries (High 1 through High 4, R17-03..R17-06), a battery of concrete filters and management rules the book insists on (a required micro trend-line break between counts, a climax veto, a spike-and-trend requirement, a trend-direction gate, a deliberate counter-trend fade when the trend is strong enough, a trading-range-boundary fade variant, an early-failure exit before a scalper's profit, a reverse-on-opposing-trigger rule, and a wider stop for small/doji signal bars), plus three hard-graded candidates borrowed from the pattern-evolution material (correction-adequacy before re-counting, requiring a countertrend micro-signal to fail before taking the with-trend continuation, and a measured-move target off a failed count's breakout bar). Three passages requiring an inverse chart, a faster timeframe, or higher-timeframe distraction are rejected as needing data the engine does not have.
